valuation_philosophy.summary: CBA is a bank, so the owner-FCF DCF is the wrong tool: operating cash flow swings tens of billions on deposit and loan flows, deposits are funding not debt, and there is no EBITDA. The value of a bank is its tangible book plus the present value of the excess it earns over its cost of equity on that book. CBA earns a cash ROTE of ~15.5% against a ~9.5% AUD cost of equity, a genuine and durable spread (#1 retail and business MFI share, lowest-cost deposit base, CET1 12.0%). Capitalising that spread gives a base value of ~$80/share, about 1.9x tangible book and 12x FY26 cash EPS. The market pays $152.33, 3.6x tangible book and 23x cash EPS: on the base flows that price is only reached at a 6.5% cost of equity, i.e. below the 10-year government bond yield plus any equity premium, or at a perpetual ROTE well above anything CBA has earned. The franchise is excellent; the price already capitalises a better one. Even the bull case (17% ROTE, 9% CoE) does not reach the current price.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost-of-equity assumption dominates: every 50bp on the CoE moves the base value ~$7-8/share (see sensitivity); superannuation flows and index weight keep the market's effective discount rate structurally low for CBA
ROTE durability: NIM under competitive pressure (2.05% FY26, 2.04% 1H26) while costs grow 8-9%; a slip to peer-level ~12-13% ROTE is the bear case
Credit cycle: FY26 impairment of 7bps of loans is a cycle low; normalisation to 15-20bps takes ~1pp off ROTE before any housing downturn
AI-enabled mortgage fraud (~A$1bn self-reported Mar-2026): enforcement, remediation and control cost are unquantified; a large AUSTRAC/ASIC penalty is a discrete downside not in the base
Capital: CET1 12.0% vs 10.25% minimum gives capacity for returns, but a buy-back at 3.6x tangible book would destroy per-share value in this model, so none is assumed

Upside risk to the valuation: the model gives no credit to the premium the market has paid for CBA for a decade; if that persists the price may never approach intrinsic value on any reasonable horizon

inputs.buyback_note: FY26 nil (FY25 $18m, 118,000 shares); $1bn program expired 12-Aug-2026 and will not be extended
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, AUD: 10y ACGB ~4.4% (Sep-2026) + beta 1.0 x AUD ERP 5.0% = 9.4%, rounded to 9.5% base; 9.0% bull (AAA sovereign, 79% deposit-funded, top-quartile capital), 10.5% bear (conduct/regulatory premium). No debt in the discount rate: residual income is post-interest.
inputs.market_implied_note: Cost of equity at which the base-case flows are worth the current price
inputs.lease_treatment: n/a -- lease liabilities (705) are immaterial against a $1.45tn balance sheet and sit inside the bank's funding
inputs.nci_treatment: none -- NTA definition excludes NCI and other equity instruments; both nil at 30-Jun-2026
inputs.notes: MODEL: residual income on tangible book, per dcf-methods routing 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift -> Residual income on tangible book'. Flows are cash NPAT = ROTE x opening TBV; dividends at the payout ratio; retention compounds TBV (clean surplus, flat shares). Residual income = NPAT - CoE x opening TBV, discounted at the cost of equity; terminal RI grows at g. Value = TBV0 + PV(RI) + PV(TV); the DDM identity (PV dividends + PV terminal equity) reproduces the same number and is asserted in the build. No owner-FCF, EBITDA, capex or net debt fields because none exist for a bank (gross_profit, EBITDA, capex, FCF deliberately NULL in Metrics.csv). Same treatment family as SOFI, SRBK and GEN.NZ. Fresh build 2026-09-22 (no prior DCF). Dashboard slider engine cannot rebuild a residual-income model from component fields; expect the non-FCF fallback.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: sustainable growth = ROTE x retention (15.5% x 25% = 3.9%), rounded down to sit between 5yr EPS CAGR (2.5%) and NTA/share CAGR (2.1%) and the 5yr DPS CAGR (7.6%, flattered by the FY21 COVID-cut base)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR is ~0% because FY21 equity (78,718) was inflated by the pre-buyback capital surplus (CET1 13.1%) that the FY22 $6bn off-market buy-back returned; per-share NTA (+2.1%/yr) and EPS (+2.5%/yr) are the meaningful series. FCF CAGRs are null by design: a bank's operating cash flow is balance-sheet flow, not free cash.
historical_growth.notes: Bank: no owner-FCF series exists. Growth is retained-earnings compounding on tangible book at the cash ROTE, which is what the residual-income model projects.

base.terminal_growth_label: residual income growth in perpetuity after year 10
base.rationale: Cash ROTE holds at the FY26 level (15.5% on opening tangible book; FY26 cash NPAT $10,982m / opening TBV $70,694m) for three years -- volume growth in business lending (+13% FY26, 1.3x system) and operating leverage offset home-loan/deposit competition -- then eases to 15.0% as loan impairment normalises from 7bps of loans (FY26 $788m) toward ~12bps and NIM drifts a few bps lower. Payout 75%, the middle of the 70-80% target range (FY26 77%). Share count flat: the $1bn buy-back lapsed 12-Aug-2026 unextended and the DRP is neutralised on-market. Cost of equity 9.5% (10y ACGB ~4.4% + 1.0 beta x 5.0% AUD ERP, +0.1 rounding). Terminal residual income grows 3.0% (sustainable growth ROTE x retention = 3.9%, haircut for a mature oligopoly at ~25% share).

bull.terminal_growth_label: residual income growth in perpetuity after year 10
bull.rationale: ROTE rises to 17% by FY31 on business-banking mix shift, GenAI-driven productivity holding the cost-to-income ratio near 45%, and impairments staying near cycle lows; cost of equity 9.0% (CBA's AAA-sovereign, top-quartile capital and deposit franchise justify a below-peer discount rate); terminal growth 3.5%.

bear.terminal_growth_label: residual income growth in perpetuity after year 10
bear.rationale: ROTE fades to 12.5% by FY30: home-loan and deposit competition compresses NIM below 2.0%, costs keep growing 8-9%/yr faster than income, the ~A$1bn AI-enabled mortgage-fraud matter brings remediation/enforcement cost and tighter origination, and a housing downturn lifts impairments to 25-30bps of loans. Payout held at 80% to defend the dividend. Cost of equity 10.5% (regulatory/conduct risk premium), terminal growth 2.5%.

base.terminal_pct_note: DDM framing: PV of (year-10 tangible book + terminal residual income) over equity value; the residual-income terminal alone is pv_terminal_residual_income / equity_value
base.implied_exit_multiple_note: year-10 terminal equity value / year-10 tangible book (P/TBV)

entry_price.methodology: Value of the same flows discounted at the 15% hurdle, with the terminal residual income also capitalised at the hurdle (CoE = 15%); no separate exit multiple
entry_price.note: At a 15% required return the residual income of a ~15% ROTE bank is negative every year, so the entry price sits below tangible book (justified P/TBV = (ROTE - g)/(r - g) < 1). That is the arithmetic, not a forecast of where the stock trades.

sensitivity.note: rows = cost of equity, columns = terminal residual-income growth; base flows (ROTE path, payout) held

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House 25/50/25. Bear not overweighted: CBA's earnings risk is margin and credit-cycle compression, not solvency (CET1 12.0%, provisioning 1.53% coverage) and the fraud matter is a cost, not a franchise break. Bull not underweighted despite the price: it is a judgment on ROTE and CoE, not on the multiple.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street bases coincide: SBC is 1.7% of NPAT and already expensed, share count flat; the band collapsed, band_position is null by design
